sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Write the function of (a) glucose (b) cellulose.
questions.answer: (a) Glucose is the main energy source (the only source for the nervous system). (b) Cellulose gives bulk to faeces and helps bowel movement.

questions.q: Match: (a) Vitamin D (b) Vitamin B1 (c) Vitamin C with (i) beri-beri (ii) scurvy (iii) rickets.
Name the deficiency disease caused by lack of (a) iron (b) iodine.
questions.answer: (a) Anaemia. (b) Goitre.

questions.q: State true or false: (a) Vitamin D can be made in the skin. (b) 1 g of fat gives more energy than 1 g of carbohydrate.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) True.

questions.q: Name two water-soluble vitamins and two fat-soluble vitamins.
questions.answer: Water-soluble: B complex and C. Fat-soluble: A, D, E and K.

questions.q: Name the two forms of PEM.
questions.answer: Kwashiorkor and marasmus.

questions.q: Which provides more energy: 100 g of sugar or 100 g of butter? Why?
questions.answer: Butter, since fats give about 9 kcal per gram while carbohydrates give about 4 kcal.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) Rickets is due to deficiency of vitamin ______. (b) The essential amino acids are those which cannot be ______ by the body.
questions.answer: (a) D. (b) synthesised.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What is PEM? Give two reasons for PEM.
questions.answer: Protein energy malnutrition, a deficiency of proteins and calories mainly in children. Reasons: a diet poor in proteins and calories due to poverty, and early weaning or infections.

questions.q: Write any two functions of roughage.
questions.answer: It helps bowel movement and prevents constipation; it helps in retaining water and in controlling blood sugar and cholesterol.

questions.q: Why does a pregnant woman need a special diet? List any four main nutrient constituents of that diet.
questions.answer: To meet the energy and growth needs of the foetus and her own health. Nutrients: proteins, iron, calcium and vitamins (folic acid) along with extra calories.

questions.q: Expand the abbreviation PEM. Write the names of two deficiency diseases caused due to PEM.
questions.answer: Protein Energy Malnutrition. Kwashiorkor and marasmus.

questions.q: Differentiate between macronutrients and micronutrients.
questions.answer: Macronutrients (carbohydrates, fats, proteins, water) are needed in large amounts; micronutrients (vitamins and minerals) in small amounts.

questions.q: Name two sources and two functions of proteins.
questions.answer: Sources: milk and pulses. Functions: growth and repair; enzymes and antibodies.

questions.q: What is a balanced diet?
questions.answer: A diet containing all nutrients in adequate amounts in the right proportion for the age, sex and work of the person.

questions.q: What is obesity? Name two disorders associated with it.
questions.answer: Excess fat deposition in the body; hypertension and heart disease.

questions.q: Write the deficiency diseases of vitamin A and vitamin D.
questions.answer: Vitamin A: night blindness and xerophthalmia. Vitamin D: rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Write the functions and sources of carbohydrates.
questions.answer: They are the cheapest source of energy, glucose fuels the nervous system, excess is stored as glycogen and fat, and cellulose gives bulk. Sources: cereals, potato, sugar, fruits and honey.

questions.q: Write the functions of fats.
questions.answer: Richest energy source, structural part of membranes, absorption of fat-soluble vitamins, hormone precursors, insulation and padding of organs.

questions.q: Write the functions of proteins with sources.
questions.answer: Growth and repair, enzymes, hormones, antibodies and transport; sources: milk, egg, fish, pulses and cereals.

questions.q: Describe the deficiency diseases caused by vitamins B1, C and D.
questions.answer: B1: beri-beri (pain in the limbs, paralysis); C: scurvy (bleeding gums, joint pain); D: rickets in children (bow legs) and osteomalacia in adults.

questions.q: Describe the functions of calcium, iron and iodine.
questions.answer: Calcium builds bones and teeth; iron forms haemoglobin; iodine is required for thyroxine.

questions.q: Differentiate between kwashiorkor and marasmus.
questions.answer: Kwashiorkor: protein deficiency; swollen belly and oedema. Marasmus: deficiency of both protein and energy; severe wasting.

questions.q: Explain the energy requirements of the body.
questions.answer: They depend on age, sex, work and physiological condition; for example 2400 kcal for a sedentary man, 4000 for heavy work, 3300 in pregnancy and 3700 during lactation.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Describe the vitamins, their sources, functions and deficiency diseases.
questions.answer: Water-soluble B complex and C; fat-soluble A, D, E and K with sources, functions and deficiency symptoms.

questions.q: Describe the classification of nutrients and the functions of proteins, carbohydrates and fats.
questions.answer: Macronutrients and micronutrients; energy, body-building and protective foods; functions of each major nutrient.

questions.q: Explain protein energy malnutrition, obesity and hypervitaminosis.
questions.answer: Kwashiorkor and marasmus with causes and symptoms; obesity from excess intake and associated diseases; hypervitaminosis from excess fat-soluble vitamins.

questions.q: Explain the role of minerals and water in the body.
questions.answer: Calcium and phosphorus for bones; iron for haemoglobin; iodine for thyroxine; sodium and potassium for fluid balance; water for transport, digestion, excretion and temperature control.
